newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants Irkutskenergo to sell energy to China.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants Irkutskenergo to sell energy to China.

text.p: First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Monday that work should be accelerated on allowing Russia's independent Irkutskenergo utility to export surplus electricity to neighbouring China.

"We're conducting work on exporting surplus electricity to China, according to which Irkutskenenergo will have the possibility of exporting surplus electricity to China," he told the Siberian Accord group of regional officials and businessmen.

"We need to speed up this work -- this is real money into the energy system," he said, referring to plans to build a $1.5 billion system allowing Irkutskenergo to export 10 billion kilowatt hours a year to Asia.
Irkutskenergo is one of two regional "energo" power plant utilities in Russia that is not partially owned by the Unified Energy System (UES) monopoly.
The two companies have in the past quarrelled over the China export plan and over ownership issues. Irkutskenergo would have to use, at least partially, UES powerlines.
The plant, based in southern Siberia, supplies the Irkutsk aluminium smelter. Its American Depositary Receipts are traded in London.
